answer_1.quote: We introduced a novel evaluation framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems based on sub-question coverage. By decomposing complex, open-ended queries into core, background, and follow-up sub-questions, we provided a more refined approach to evaluating RAG-generated responses.
answer_1.outputs: long-form answers to open-ended and non-factoid questions

answer_2.quote: We introduce a weighted metric for evaluating answers that outperforms the conventional LLM-as-a-judge approach and strongly correlates with human preferences for open-ended answers.
automatic_metrics: capability to identify core knowledge from retrieved chunks
potential of getting performance gain by improving retrieval for core sub-questions
correlation between core sub-question coverage and knowledge appearance frequency
position alignment with human writing habit

answer_3.quote: We rely on GPT-4 Judge as the evaluator, despite it being less effective than our proposed answer quality metrics, because it is widely used in prior works and evaluation libraries.

answer_4.quote: We recruit five human annotators to manually classify 200 sub-questions into three types of sub-questions, and we take the majority vote of the annotations as the ground-truth type.
answer_4.guideline: We prompt GPT-4 with few-shot annotated examples to automatically measure the sub-question coverage... we compared GPT-4's automatic judgments with human annotations on 100 samples, finding an 83% alignment rate.
